domains.name: Communication, Relationships & Cultural Humility
domains.description: Measures the interpersonal core of CHW practice: plain-language health communication, active listening and comprehension checks, trust and rapport with professional boundaries, motivational interviewing, and cultural responsiveness and humility in every client interaction.

domains.name: Outreach & Service Navigation
domains.description: Measures connecting people to care: field-based outreach to communities with historical mistrust of systems, matching client needs to community resources, referrals and follow-up, resource directories, and coordinating care across providers and agencies.

domains.name: Education & Capacity Building
domains.description: Measures teaching and empowerment: delivering culturally and literacy-appropriate health education, facilitating participatory group learning, conveying evidence-based information without bias, and building client and community capacity toward independence.

domains.name: Advocacy & Assessment
domains.description: Measures speaking up and seeing clearly: individual and systems-level advocacy, coaching clients toward self-advocacy, structured and informal needs assessment, identifying social determinants of health, and recognizing community assets alongside gaps.

domains.name: Professional Practice, Ethics & Evaluation
domains.description: Measures the professional foundation: confidentiality, documentation accuracy and timeliness, boundary management and supervision, reliability, mandated reporting, program data collection, and understanding evaluation — outputs versus outcomes and data quality.

subdomains.name: Communication
subdomains.description: Plain-language explanation, active listening, comprehension confirmation, adapting communication mode, and empathetic non-judgmental language.

subdomains.name: Interpersonal and relationship building
subdomains.description: Trust through consistency and follow-through, motivational interviewing, working with ambivalence, professional boundaries with genuine rapport, and reading emotional cues.

subdomains.name: Cultural responsiveness and humility
subdomains.description: Awareness of one's own cultural identity and biases, understanding each client's values without assumptions, culturally adapting services, language access, and ongoing self-reflection.

subdomains.name: Service coordination and navigation
subdomains.description: Matching needs to resources, helping clients schedule and complete referrals, follow-up to confirm connection, resource directories, and multi-agency care coordination.

subdomains.name: Outreach
subdomains.description: Field-based engagement where people live, work, and gather; trust-building with populations that mistrust systems; motivating enrollment; overcoming outreach barriers; and accurate contact tracking.

subdomains.name: Education and facilitation
subdomains.description: Culture- and literacy-appropriate health education, participatory group facilitation, unbiased evidence-based content, real-time delivery adjustment, and evaluating whether sessions met objectives.

subdomains.name: Capacity building
subdomains.description: Teaching independence skills, strengths-based practice, facilitating community participation, supporting client-owned goals, and stepping back as capacity grows.

subdomains.name: Advocacy
subdomains.description: Speaking up for clients facing barriers, surfacing systemic issues to supervisors, coaching self-advocacy, documenting service gaps and inequities, and representing client interests in community settings.

subdomains.name: Individual and community assessment
subdomains.description: Structured and informal needs assessment, identifying social determinants of health, clear and confidential documentation of findings, triaging immediate versus long-term needs, and mapping community assets.

subdomains.name: Professional skills and ethical conduct
subdomains.description: Confidentiality across all channels, accurate and timely documentation, boundary management with supervision, reliability, and mandated reporting.

subdomains.name: Evaluation and research
subdomains.description: Accurate program data collection, understanding metrics and their purpose, participating in evaluation activities, outputs versus outcomes, and flagging data quality issues.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain health information using plain, jargon-free language appropriate to the client's literacy level.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing wording a client can act on and recognizing when medical jargon or reading level blocks understanding.

competencies.statement: The learner can use active listening techniques — eye contact, paraphrasing, open-ended questions — during client interactions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting listening behaviors that draw the client out rather than closed questions or premature advice.

competencies.statement: The learner can confirm client understanding by asking the client to restate key information.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by applying teach-back correctly and distinguishing it from simply asking "do you understand?".

competencies.statement: The learner can adapt communication style — verbal, written, visual — based on client needs and preferences.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by matching the communication mode to the client's literacy, language, sensory, and situational needs.

competencies.statement: The learner can demonstrate empathy and non-judgmental language when discussing sensitive topics.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing responses that normalize and support rather than shame, lecture, or minimize.

competencies.statement: The learner can establish trust with clients through consistent, respectful, follow-through behavior.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing that kept commitments and reliability, not credentials, build trust with clients.

competencies.statement: The learner can use motivational interviewing techniques: reflective listening, affirmations, and change talk.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by identifying and applying MI responses that evoke the client's own motivation rather than directing.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify and address client ambivalence toward behavior change without directing or pressuring.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by rolling with ambivalence, exploring both sides, and avoiding the righting reflex.

competencies.statement: The learner can maintain appropriate professional boundaries while building genuine rapport.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by distinguishing warmth from over-involvement, such as gifts, personal loans, or off-hours contact.

competencies.statement: The learner can recognize and respond appropriately to client emotional cues and body language.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by noticing nonverbal signals of distress, withdrawal, or discomfort and adjusting the interaction.

competencies.statement: The learner can demonstrate awareness of their own cultural identity, biases, and how these affect client interactions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing bias in scenarios and describing how the CHW's own lens shapes what they assume.

competencies.statement: The learner can seek to understand each client's cultural values, beliefs, and practices without making assumptions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by asking rather than assuming, and avoiding stereotype-based service decisions.

competencies.statement: The learner can adapt services — education, outreach, navigation — to reflect the cultural context of the population served.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by adjusting materials, examples, settings, and messengers to fit the community's cultural context.

competencies.statement: The learner can use language access resources — interpretation and translation — appropriately and consistently.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing qualified interpretation over ad-hoc solutions like family members, especially children.

competencies.statement: The learner can commit to ongoing self-reflection and learning about cultures represented in the service community.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by treating cultural humility as continuous practice rather than a completed training.

competencies.statement: The learner can accurately identify client needs and match them to appropriate community resources.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting the resource that fits the client's actual need, eligibility, and access constraints.

competencies.statement: The learner can assist clients in scheduling appointments, completing referral forms, and navigating systems.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by walking a client through concrete navigation steps while building their ability to do it themselves.

competencies.statement: The learner can follow up on referrals to confirm client connection and address barriers.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by treating a referral as complete only when the client connected, and troubleshooting when they did not.

competencies.statement: The learner can maintain a current, organized resource directory relevant to the service population.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by keeping resource information verified and current rather than passing on stale or wrong details.

competencies.statement: The learner can coordinate care across multiple providers or agencies on behalf of the client.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by sequencing communication among providers, with consent, so services connect instead of duplicating.

competencies.statement: The learner can engage community members in settings where they live, work, or gather.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing field-based engagement approaches suited to the setting and population.

competencies.statement: The learner can use trust-building strategies appropriate for populations with historical mistrust of systems.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing why mistrust is reasonable and selecting approaches that earn credibility over time.

competencies.statement: The learner can communicate program offerings clearly and motivate eligible individuals to enroll or engage.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by framing benefits concretely and honestly without overpromising or pressuring.

competencies.statement: The learner can overcome common outreach barriers — language, transportation, mistrust — with appropriate strategies.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by matching a barrier to a workable strategy rather than treating non-engagement as client failure.

competencies.statement: The learner can track outreach contacts, encounters, and follow-ups accurately in program records.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recording encounters completely and promptly so the program's outreach picture stays true.

competencies.statement: The learner can deliver health education using materials and methods appropriate to the audience's culture and literacy.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting materials and delivery methods that fit the audience rather than defaulting to clinical handouts.

competencies.statement: The learner can facilitate group learning sessions using participatory techniques — discussion, role-play, Q&A.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing facilitation moves that make participants active contributors rather than passive listeners.

competencies.statement: The learner can accurately convey evidence-based health information without adding personal bias.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by separating evidence from opinion and referring questions beyond CHW scope to licensed providers.

competencies.statement: The learner can adjust content delivery in real time based on participant response or comprehension.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by reading confusion or disengagement mid-session and changing pace, examples, or method.

competencies.statement: The learner can evaluate whether education sessions met learning objectives using pre/post questions or observation.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by choosing a feasible check of learning rather than assuming attendance equals understanding.

competencies.statement: The learner can teach clients skills that increase their independence, such as self-monitoring and system navigation.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by doing with rather than doing for, so the client can repeat the skill without the CHW.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify and build on client and community strengths rather than focusing solely on deficits.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by naming existing assets and skills as the foundation of a plan instead of leading with problems.

competencies.statement: The learner can facilitate community members' participation in planning or problem-solving processes.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by structuring processes so community members shape decisions rather than receive them.

competencies.statement: The learner can support clients in setting and tracking their own health or wellness goals.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by eliciting client-owned goals and simple tracking rather than assigning CHW-chosen targets.

competencies.statement: The learner can recognize when a client has built capacity and adjust the level of support accordingly.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by stepping back as independence grows instead of maintaining dependence on the CHW.

competencies.statement: The learner can speak up on behalf of individual clients when they face barriers to care or services.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by advocating effectively and respectfully within systems when a client is wrongly denied or delayed.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify systemic or policy-level issues affecting the community and communicate them to supervisors.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by distinguishing one-off problems from patterns and routing patterns to the right level.

competencies.statement: The learner can support clients in self-advocacy by coaching them before appointments or interactions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by preparing clients to speak for themselves rather than speaking in their place by default.

competencies.statement: The learner can document and report patterns of service gaps or inequities appropriately.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recording gaps factually and reporting them through appropriate channels.

competencies.statement: The learner can participate in community meetings or coalitions as a representative of client interests.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by carrying client and community perspectives into coalition settings within the CHW role.

competencies.statement: The learner can conduct structured or informal needs assessments using validated tools or guided questions.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by selecting and applying an assessment approach suited to the client and setting.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify social determinants of health affecting the client or community.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing housing, food, transportation, income, and safety factors behind presenting problems.

competencies.statement: The learner can document assessment findings clearly, accurately, and confidentially.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by writing findings that are factual and complete while protecting client privacy.

competencies.statement: The learner can distinguish between immediate needs and longer-term social or health barriers.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by triaging urgent needs first while keeping longer-term barriers on the plan.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify community assets — organizations, leaders, programs — alongside gaps and needs.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by mapping what a community has, not only what it lacks.

competencies.statement: The learner can maintain strict client confidentiality in all written, verbal, and digital communications.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing confidentiality breaches across channels — hallway talk, texts, social media, records.

competencies.statement: The learner can complete required documentation accurately and within designated timeframes.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by documenting encounters factually and on time so records support care and program integrity.

competencies.statement: The learner can recognize and manage professional boundary issues, seeking supervision when needed.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by spotting boundary drift early and bringing it to supervision rather than handling it alone.

competencies.statement: The learner can demonstrate reliability: punctual, prepared, and following through on commitments to clients and team.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by treating reliability as a clinical skill — missed commitments damage client trust and care.

competencies.statement: The learner can apply mandated reporting requirements appropriately and without hesitation when required.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by recognizing reportable situations and following the required process even when relationships are at stake.

competencies.statement: The learner can collect program data accurately using required forms, databases, or electronic systems.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by entering complete, correct data in the required system at the required time.

competencies.statement: The learner can explain the purpose of program metrics and how individual data contributes to outcomes.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by connecting their own data entry to program funding, quality, and community impact.

competencies.statement: The learner can participate in program evaluation activities such as surveys, focus groups, and data review meetings.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by contributing field insight to evaluation activities constructively.

competencies.statement: The learner can describe the difference between outputs (activities) and outcomes (changes) in CHW programs.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by classifying examples correctly — encounters and classes held versus blood pressure controlled or housing secured.

competencies.statement: The learner can identify and communicate data quality issues — missing data, errors — to the appropriate person.
competencies.description: Demonstrated by flagging rather than ignoring or silently fixing suspect data.
